A09 · FT-49 · behaviour tier

Phone text entry and repeated taps

iPhone Safari zooms in when you tap a text box whose text is under 16 px, and it treats a quick second tap on a button as "zoom". Both match your three reports. Measured on the phone in Manage:

PageBoxes under 16 pxTodayProposed
Identity (Honour, Glory, Status, Taint: Rank and Points)814 px16 px
Rings & Traits (Water mastery picker)113.3 px16 px
Skills (name, Trait, Rank)15 of 1614.7 px16 px
Advantages (description)214.4 px16 px
Techniques (Advanced School picker)114.7 px16 px
Every button and stepper on the page127double-tap zoomsdouble-tap presses twice

Your three iPhone reports, and what changes

ReportCauseAfter the change
A quick double press on − / + zooms instead of pressing twiceButtons let Safari's double-tap zoom throughButtons and steppers press twice. Double-tap on text or empty space still zooms.
Typing in a box zooms in and stays zoomedBox text under 16 pxNo zoom on tapping a box.
Double-tap sometimes will not zoom back outMostly the zoom from the box above, then a double-tap that lands on a controlThe box zoom no longer happens. Double-tap on text or empty space zooms out; pinch works everywhere.

Laptop: no change. The rules apply only at phone widths and on touch screens. Pinch zoom stays everywhere, and the page's zoom is never forced back.

Recommend: approve. FT-49 counts as fixed only after your device check on Safari and the installed app, all three cases.

A10 · FT-50, FT-52 · behaviour tier

Cross-page actions move focus

The row. On a laptop the button sits 4 px below its hint (FT-50, your Edge note). Proposed: the hint and button share one row, centred on each other. On a phone the hint fills the line, so the button wraps below it at its 44 px height, as today.

Focus (FT-52). You cannot see this part; keyboards and screen readers rely on it.

After tapping Go to Advanced SchoolsTodayProposed
Where focus isStill on the button, on the hidden Identity pageThe "Advanced School" heading on Techniques
Identity pageStays live behind TechniquesInert, like any page you are not on
Next Tab key (laptop)Honour Rank on the hidden Identity pageThe Advanced School picker
Phone keyboardDoes not openDoes not open (a heading is not a text box)
Going backTap the Identity tabThe same

Go to Advanced Schools is the only button today that opens another page. The new rule is written once and used there, so any later cross-page button can use it too.

Recommend: approve.

A10.1 (proposed id) · your 12 November item · behaviour tier

The gold outline after the School-choice window

The outline is the page's keyboard-focus ring. When the window closes it gives focus back to what had it before. On an iPhone that is the page, because Safari does not focus a tapped button. Reproduced in this test browser:

A · draw the page ring only for the keyboard (recommended)

The ring shows when you reach a page with the Tab key, never after a tap or a window closing. It covers every window in the app at once, and focus still goes back where it was.

B · give focus back to the button that opened the window

Each window would need its own change. On an iPhone, Safari may then draw a smaller ring on that button instead.

Recommend: A. A unit of its own, next to A10, so either can be removed alone.

A17 · FT-41 · behaviour tier (startup)

Fill the splash without cutting off the title

Today the artwork is shown whole (contain) on its paper colour, so any screen that does not match one of the three pictures gets paper bands. Proposed: the artwork fills the screen (cover), with a focal point chosen for each picture so the title and the scroll stay in view. The square picture is used up to 3 : 2 instead of 4 : 3, because a laptop window around 1440 × 1000 keeps more of the picture that way.

Unchanged: the first paint, the 5-second hold, the tap guard, and how the splash leaves when the sheet is ready or reports an error. Only the picture's fit and which picture shows change.

A18 · investigation

The first Manage tap on an iPhone

Not reproduced here. Time from the tap to the screen showing Manage, phone size, three fresh starts each:

Test browserFirst tapSecond tap
Normal speed45–62 ms37–50 ms
Slowed 4×140–179 ms185–224 ms

The first tap is not slower than the second. An iPhone can still differ, so the audit asks for a measurement on your phone before any fix.

  1. Quick check (no build): on the live app, open a character, tap Manage. Does the first tap still feel slow? If not, A18 closes as not reproduced, with these numbers and your answer.
  2. Only if it does: a throwaway timing preview, never merged, that shows on screen the milliseconds from tap to Manage for the first and second tap. You do three fresh starts and send a screenshot. Only a demonstrated slow step gets fixed.

Recommend: this two-step check. You can do step 1 any time before the device round.
